a: Yes. Downloading the app is free, and so is a lot of what's inside: the daily affirmation and its reminder, the home screen widget, your journal, the Help page, 2 articles in every topic, and 20 coping skills in the Pocketbook. Anxious Black Girls Plus is an optional subscription that unlocks the rest.

q: What comes with Anxious Black Girls Plus?
a: Plus unlocks every article in all 22 topics (with audio as it's added), all 57 coping skills in the Pocketbook, skill videos, a practice space for every skill where you can work through it and save your practices, and your own reminders for meds, meals, tasks, and the texts you keep forgetting to answer. Your subscription also supports a Black woman-owned mental health company.

Plus comes as a monthly or a yearly plan, and the yearly plan costs less over a full year. You'll see the current price in your currency on the Plus page before you buy. To get there, go to Help, then Anxious Black Girls Plus, or tap the Plus button on any locked article or skill. Payment goes through your Apple Account.

On your iPhone, open the Settings app, tap your name, then Subscriptions, then Anxious Black Girls, then Cancel Subscription. You can also tap Manage subscription on the Plus page. Cancel at least 24 hours before your renewal date to avoid the next charge. You keep Plus until the end of the time you already paid for.

q: I paid for Plus, but things are still locked. What do I do?
a: Go to the Plus page and tap Restore purchases. Make sure you're signed in with the same Apple Account you used to subscribe. This also brings Plus back after you get a new phone or reinstall the app.
Apple handles every payment, so we can't see your purchase or issue refunds ourselves. You can ask Apple for a refund at reportaproblem.apple.com.

q: Do I need to create an account?
a: No. There's nothing to sign up for. Plus is tied to your Apple Account, and we never see your name, email, or card details.

Only you. Your entries are saved on your phone and never sent to us or anyone else. We can't read them, even if you ask us to. To add a lock, go to Help, then Privacy and settings, and turn on Face ID or your passcode.

q: What happens to my journal if I delete the app or get a new phone?
a: Your entries are erased, because they only live on your phone. To keep a copy, open the Journal and tap "Copy all entries," then paste them into your Notes app or an email to yourself.

q: Where do I find the skills I saved?
a: Tap [Saved](#saved) at the bottom of the screen, then scroll to "My pocketbook." Every skill you tapped "Save to my pocketbook" on lives there, along with your saved affirmations and articles. Practices you save are right below, under "My practices," and on each skill's page.

q: Why did my saved affirmations and skills disappear?
a: Saved items live on your phone inside the app. Deleting the app, or tapping Delete everything under Help, Privacy and settings, removes them for good.

q: How do I add today's affirmation to my home screen?
a: Touch and hold an empty spot on your Home Screen, tap Edit, then Add Widget. Search for Anxious Black Girls and pick a size. You can add it to your Lock Screen the same way. Widgets need iOS 17 or newer. You can also get it as a daily notification: go to Help, then Privacy and settings, turn on the Daily affirmation reminder and pick a time.

q: Does the app work without internet?
a: Yes. Affirmations, articles, audio, and coping skills are stored inside the app, so they work offline. Links to outside websites and phone calls need a connection or cell service.

No. The app offers education and encouragement. It doesn't diagnose or treat any condition and doesn't replace care from a licensed professional. If you're looking for a therapist, see the therapist options on this Help page or visit our About page.

q: Does anyone monitor what I write or read?
a: No. Nobody watches the app in real time. If you're in crisis, call 911 or call/text 988.

q: Where do the articles come from?
a: Every article is written for Black women and backed by published research, listed under Sources at the end. They're for learning, not for diagnosing yourself.

q: How often is new content added?
a: A new affirmation and journal prompt appear every day. New articles, audio, and topics arrive through app updates, so keep automatic updates on in the App Store.

q: I found a problem or have an idea. Who do I contact?
a: Email us at support@anxiousblackgirls.com. We'll get back to you as soon as we can. This inbox isn't monitored for emergencies. If you're in crisis, call 911 or call/text 988.
